dana_csm: Hey team — Acme Prod on us is seeing a spike of 500s from /v1/embeddings between ~02:30-02:45 PST. Customer is on the phone. They say requests return 500 with 'upstream process exited'.
ben_sre: Copy. can you paste 1-3 failing request IDs and region?
dana_csm: reqs: r_3a9f2, r_3a9f3, r_3a9f7. Region: us-west-2. CS log shows '503 -> 500: upstream exit code 137' and a restart of the host.
carla_runtime: I pulled the host logs (pool-host-218). Repeated process restarts ~02:34. nvml log: "E: RTX: out of memory when allocating 1310720000 bytes" and one entry with 'illegal instruction' right before restart. Snip:
```
E0304 02:34:12 runtime.cu: alloc failed: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
E0304 02:34:12 nvml-monitor: out_of_memory on GPU0
runtime: worker pid 21456 exited with code 137
---
signal: illegal instruction at 0x7f9c2b1a
core dumped: /var/crash/worker-21456.core
```
ben_sre: I'm going to drain pool-host-218 and route Acme traffic to fallback embed pool. Doing now.
deploy_bot: routing change submitted: acme-prod -> fallback-embed-pool (immediate).
opsbot: routing change applied for tenant acme-prod (5m).
carla_runtime: Quick hypothesis: large embed payloads + aggressive kv-prefetch + dynbatch growth caused per-worker memory balloon. Prefetch/kv cache wasn't bounded and we saw >10GB growth prior to OOM.
carla_runtime: Repro steps I used locally: 1) send the customer payload (multidoc with 512k tokens) in batch=32 to local runtime; 2) observe kv cache growth via /debug/kvcache; 3) trigger embed-heavy toolcall -> see mem climb then OOM. Curl example:
```
curl -X POST https://api.internal/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." -d '{"inputs": ["<huge_doc_1>", "<huge_doc_2>"], "model":"embed-xxl"}'
```
ben_sre: Good repro. Mitigation plan: 1) cap per-request prefetch memory to 512MB via runtime flag; 2) add backpressure so dynbatch cannot grow beyond N workers; 3) enable fallback routing for any tenant hitting repeated OOMs. Can we hotpatch flag?
carla_runtime: I'll build a canary image with PREFETCH_MAX_BYTES=536870912 and a dynbatch ceiling for one host. Rolling canary to pool-host-219; if stable, roll to pool-host-218 after drain. ETA ~2h for image + canary.
dana_csm: Noted. Told Acme we can route them to a dedicated instance while we hotpatch; they accepted.
ben_sre: Also requested core dumps + cuda-smi snapshots from the affected host before it's recycled. Carla, can you collect those and attach to the ticket?
carla_runtime: Will do. grabbing /var/crash/worker-21456.core, nvml logs, and dmesg; uploading to ticket INC-38221.
dana_csm: CS updated customer and logged impact windows. customer asked whether this is related to recent quantization rollout — they sent a sample.
carla_runtime: Checked: the failing hosts had mixed bins (one quantized model swapped in yesterday). I don't see immediate correlation but will repro with quantized artifact too.
ben_sre: For immediate relief, ops changed routing and draining host-218. If canary passes we hotpatch widely and then revert routing.
dana_csm: Thx. Customer satisfied with dedicated fallback for now. :thumbsup:
carla_runtime: Follow-up checklist: collect core + nvml snapshots, run local repro with quantized artifact, push canary, monitor p95 latency and memory metrics for 30m. Owner: carla_runtime. ETA patch: ~2h.
ben_sre: I'll leave this thread open. If we see any 'illegal instruction' repeat, escalate to hw/driver guild.
opsbot: monitor_alert: GPU memory usage spike > 90% on pool-host-220 at 02:50 — alerting on-call.
